_note: Seeded into SQLite on launch. Bump content_version after edits. Each level = finite list of scenes. Each scene: situation + choices (each with its own 'effect' = what happens to the patient) + optional actions (gesture minigames that perform the correct procedure). ALL medical content must be reviewed by a qualified first-aid instructor before the pilot.

levels.title: Minor Cuts
levels.summary: Clean, protect and cover a small scrape.
levels.scenario: You fell while running and scraped your knee. It is bleeding a little and has some dirt in it.

scenes.title: Clean
scenes.situation: The scrape on your knee is dirty and bleeding a little.
scenes.prompt: What is the first thing you should do?

choices.label: Wash hands, then rinse the wound with clean water
choices.effect: The dirt washes away and the wound is ready for care. Clean hands keep germs out.

choices.label: Put a bandage on it right away
choices.effect: Dirt gets trapped under the bandage. Two days later the knee is red, swollen and painful - it got infected.

choices.label: Rub coffee grounds on it to stop the bleeding
choices.effect: Coffee grounds are not clean. Germs get into the wound and it becomes infected.

actions.title: Clean the wound
actions.instruction: Drag the right item onto the wound, then wipe left and right to clean it.
actions.hint: Clean running water is best for rinsing a small wound.

tools.label: Rubbing alcohol
tools.effect: It stings badly and damages the healthy tissue around the wound. Healing slows down.

tools.label: Coffee grounds
tools.effect: Coffee grounds are not clean. Germs get into the wound and it becomes infected.

scenes.title: Protect
scenes.situation: The wound is clean and the bleeding has stopped.
scenes.prompt: How do you protect the wound?

choices.label: Apply a thin layer of petroleum jelly or antibiotic ointment
choices.effect: The wound stays moist and protected, so it heals faster with less scarring.

choices.label: Pour hydrogen peroxide or alcohol on it
choices.effect: It stings and damages healthy tissue. The wound takes longer to heal.

actions.title: Apply ointment
actions.instruction: Drag the right item onto the wound.
actions.hint: A thin layer of petroleum jelly or antibiotic ointment.

items.label: Toothpaste
items.effect: Toothpaste irritates the wound. It is not a first-aid product.

scenes.title: Bandage
scenes.situation: The wound is clean and protected.
scenes.prompt: What do you cover it with?

choices.label: A clean, sterile bandage
choices.effect: The bandage keeps dirt and germs out while the wound heals.

choices.label: A leaf from the garden
choices.effect: Leaves carry dirt and germs. The wound gets infected.

actions.title: Bandage the wound
actions.instruction: Drag the bandage to cover the wound.
actions.hint: Use a clean, sterile bandage.

items.label: Used tissue paper
items.effect: Used tissue is full of germs. The wound gets infected.

tips: Wash your hands before touching a wound.
If it is bleeding, press a clean cloth on it until it stops.
Rinse the wound with clean running water to remove dirt.
Apply a thin layer of petroleum jelly or antibiotic ointment.
Cover with a clean bandage and change it daily or when it gets wet or dirty.
See a health worker if bleeding does not stop after 10 minutes of pressure, the cut is deep, or you see redness, swelling, pus or fever.

levels.title: Nosebleed
levels.summary: Lean forward and pinch - never tilt the head back.
levels.scenario: Your classmate suddenly has a nosebleed during recess. They look scared.

scenes.title: Position
scenes.situation: Blood is dripping from your classmate's nose.

choices.label: Sit up and lean slightly forward
choices.effect: Blood drains out of the nose instead of down the throat. They can breathe and stay calm.

choices.label: Tilt the head back
choices.effect: Blood runs down the throat. They start coughing and feel like vomiting.

choices.label: Lie down flat on the floor
choices.effect: Blood flows into the throat. They choke and cough.

actions.title: Lean forward
actions.instruction: Swipe DOWN to help them lean slightly forward.
actions.hint: Forward, not backward!
actions.success: Leaning forward keeps blood out of the throat.

params.wrong_feedback: You tilted the head back. Blood runs down the throat and they start coughing.

scenes.title: Pinch
scenes.situation: They are leaning forward, but the nose is still bleeding.
scenes.prompt: How do you stop the bleeding?

choices.label: Pinch the soft part of the nose for 10-15 minutes
choices.effect: Steady pressure lets a clot form. The bleeding slows down.

choices.label: Stuff tissue deep into the nose
choices.effect: The tissue irritates the inside of the nose, and the bleeding starts again when it is pulled out.

choices.label: Pinch for a few seconds and keep checking
choices.effect: Letting go too early breaks the clot that is forming. The bleeding continues.

actions.title: Pinch the nose
actions.instruction: Press and HOLD to pinch the soft part of the nose. Don't let go!
actions.hint: Pinch below the bony bridge and keep steady pressure.

params.release_feedback: You let go early - the clot broke and the bleeding restarted. Keep pinching.

scenes.title: Aftercare
scenes.situation: After 10 minutes, the bleeding has stopped.

choices.label: Rest and avoid blowing the nose for a few hours
choices.effect: The clot stays in place and the nosebleed does not come back.

choices.label: Blow the nose hard to clear it
choices.effect: The clot is blown out and the nose starts bleeding again.

tips: Sit up and lean slightly forward. Do NOT tilt the head back.
Pinch the soft part of the nose for 10-15 minutes without letting go.
Breathe through the mouth.
Avoid blowing the nose or heavy activity for several hours.
Get medical help if bleeding lasts more than 20 minutes, follows a head injury, or there is trouble breathing.

levels.title: Sprain
levels.scenario: While playing basketball, your friend twisted their ankle. It is swollen and painful, but they can move their toes.

scenes.title: Rest
scenes.situation: Your friend is sitting on the court holding their swollen ankle.

choices.label: Stop playing and rest the ankle
choices.effect: Resting prevents more damage to the injured ligament.

choices.label: Tell them to walk it off
choices.effect: Walking on it stretches the injured ligament even more. The pain and swelling get worse.

actions.title: RICE order
actions.instruction: Tap the RICE steps in the correct order.
actions.hint: R - I - C - E

params.prompt: Put the RICE steps in order:

distractors.label: Heat
distractors.effect: Heat increases blood flow, so a fresh sprain swells even more.

scenes.title: Ice
scenes.situation: The ankle is getting more swollen.
scenes.prompt: How do you cool the ankle?

choices.label: Ice pack wrapped in a cloth for 15-20 minutes
choices.effect: The cold reduces swelling and numbs the pain without hurting the skin.

choices.label: Hot water bottle
choices.effect: Heat increases blood flow. The ankle swells even more.

choices.label: Ice cubes directly on the skin
choices.effect: Direct ice can cause a cold injury to the skin.

actions.title: Hold the ice
actions.instruction: HOLD the wrapped ice pack on the ankle.
actions.hint: Ice for about 15-20 minutes at a time.

params.release_feedback: Keep the ice on for the full 15-20 minutes.

scenes.title: Wrap
scenes.situation: The ankle needs support.

choices.label: Elastic bandage, snug but not too tight
choices.effect: Compression limits swelling while blood keeps flowing to the foot.

choices.label: As tight as possible
choices.effect: Too tight cuts off blood flow. The toes turn pale, cold and numb.

actions.title: Wrap the ankle
actions.instruction: Draw circles around the ankle to wrap the compression bandage.
actions.hint: Toes should stay warm and pink.

scenes.title: Elevate
scenes.situation: The ankle is wrapped.
scenes.prompt: How should they rest the leg?

choices.label: Raise the ankle above heart level
choices.effect: Fluid drains away and the swelling goes down.

choices.label: Let the foot hang down
choices.effect: Fluid collects in the ankle and it swells even more.

actions.title: Elevate
actions.instruction: Swipe UP to raise the ankle above heart level.
actions.hint: Prop the leg on pillows.

params.wrong_feedback: Raise the leg UP, above the level of the heart.

tips: Rest: stop the activity and avoid putting weight on the injury.
Ice: apply a wrapped ice pack for 15-20 minutes at a time.
Compression: wrap with an elastic bandage - snug, not tight.
Elevation: raise the injured part above heart level.
Get medical help if they cannot bear weight, the joint looks deformed, or there is numbness.

levels.title: Minor Burn
levels.summary: Cool running water for 20 minutes. No toothpaste, no ice.
levels.scenario: While helping cook, your forearm touched a hot pot. The skin is red and painful. There is no big blister.

scenes.title: Cool
scenes.situation: Your forearm is red and stinging from the hot pot.

choices.label: Remove watches/rings and cool the burn under cool running water
choices.effect: The burning stops and the pain eases. Removing tight items early stops them getting stuck when the skin swells.

choices.label: Put toothpaste on it
choices.effect: Toothpaste traps heat in the skin. The burn gets deeper and may become infected.

choices.label: Put ice cubes on it
choices.effect: Ice damages the burned skin and makes the injury worse.

actions.title: Remove watch
actions.instruction: Swipe RIGHT to slide off the watch before the arm swells.
actions.hint: Remove watches, rings and tight items early.

params.wrong_feedback: Slide the watch off - swipe RIGHT.

actions.title: Cool the burn
actions.instruction: HOLD the arm under the cool running water.
actions.hint: Keep cooling for about 20 minutes.

params.release_feedback: Keep the burn under cool water for the full 20 minutes.

scenes.title: Cover
scenes.situation: After cooling, the pain is much better. The skin is still red.
scenes.prompt: How do you cover the burn?

choices.label: Loosely, with cling film or a clean non-stick dressing
choices.effect: The burn stays clean and protected without sticking.

choices.label: With cotton balls
choices.effect: Cotton fibers stick to the burn and are painful to remove.

choices.label: Pop any blisters first, then cover
choices.effect: Popping blisters opens the skin to germs. The burn gets infected.

actions.title: Cover loosely
actions.instruction: Drag the right dressing onto the burn.
actions.hint: Use something clean that will not stick.

items.label: Butter
items.effect: Butter holds heat in the skin and can cause infection.

items.label: Tight bandage
items.effect: Burns swell. A tight bandage squeezes the skin and hurts.

scenes.title: Get help
scenes.situation: Your friend asks when a burn needs a doctor.
scenes.prompt: When should you get medical help for a burn?

choices.label: If it is bigger than the palm, or on the face, hands, feet or genitals
choices.effect: Right! These burns need a health worker. Getting help early prevents complications.

choices.label: Never - burns always heal on their own
choices.effect: Large or deep burns can get infected and leave serious scars without treatment.

tips: Cool the burn under cool running water for about 20 minutes.
Remove rings, watches and tight clothing near the burn early.
Never use ice, toothpaste, butter or oil on a burn.
Do not pop blisters.
Cover loosely with a clean non-stick dressing or cling film.
Get medical help for burns larger than the person's palm, on the face, hands, feet or genitals, chemical or electrical burns, or burns on young children.

levels.title: Insect Sting
levels.summary: Remove the stinger, wash, cool - and watch for allergy.
levels.scenario: A bee stung your little brother on the arm in the garden. You can see the stinger in the skin.

scenes.title: Stinger
scenes.situation: The bee stinger is still in his arm.
scenes.prompt: How do you remove the stinger?

choices.label: Scrape it out sideways with a flat edge, like a card
choices.effect: The stinger comes out quickly, so less venom gets in.

choices.label: Squeeze it out with your fingers
choices.effect: Squeezing can push more venom into the skin. The swelling and pain get worse.

choices.label: Leave it in
choices.effect: The stinger keeps releasing venom. The sting becomes more swollen and painful.

actions.title: Scrape
actions.instruction: Swipe sideways (left or right) twice to scrape the stinger out.
actions.hint: Scrape, don't squeeze.

params.wrong_feedback: Scrape SIDEWAYS across the skin with a flat edge.

scenes.title: Wash & cool
scenes.situation: The stinger is out. The area is red and itchy.

choices.label: Wash with soap and water, then apply a cold pack
choices.effect: The area is clean and the cold reduces swelling and pain.

choices.label: Rub mud on it
choices.effect: Mud is dirty. The sting gets infected.

actions.title: Wash
actions.instruction: Drag the right item onto the sting, then wipe to wash it.
actions.hint: Soap and water.

tools.label: Mud
tools.effect: Mud is dirty. The sting gets infected.

actions.title: Cold pack
actions.instruction: Drag the right item onto the sting to reduce swelling.
actions.hint: Something cold, wrapped in cloth.

items.label: Hot compress
items.effect: Heat makes the swelling and itching worse.

scenes.title: Allergy
scenes.situation: A few minutes later, his lips start swelling and he is having trouble breathing.

choices.label: Call 911 right away - this may be a severe allergic reaction
choices.effect: Help is on the way. If he has an epinephrine auto-injector, help him use it.

choices.label: Give him water and wait
choices.effect: Severe allergic reactions get worse fast. Waiting can be life-threatening.

tips: Remove the stinger quickly - scrape it off with a flat edge.
Wash the area with soap and water.
Apply a cold pack wrapped in cloth to reduce swelling.
Call 911 if there is swelling of the face, lips or throat, trouble breathing, or dizziness.
If the person has a prescribed epinephrine auto-injector, help them use it.

levels.title: Fainting
levels.summary: Lay them down, raise the legs, check breathing.
levels.scenario: During a flag ceremony on a hot morning, a student suddenly collapses.

scenes.title: Check
scenes.situation: A student is lying on the ground and is not moving.

choices.label: Make sure the area is safe, then tap and shout to check response
choices.effect: You are safe to help, and you quickly learn how the student is doing.

choices.label: Pour water on their face
choices.effect: Water can go into the nose and mouth and make them choke.

actions.title: Check steps
actions.instruction: Tap the actions in the correct order.
actions.hint: Safety first, then response, then breathing.

params.prompt: What do you do, in order?
order: Ask someone to call 911 if they don't wake up

distractors.label: Give them water to drink
distractors.effect: Someone who is not fully awake can choke on a drink.

scenes.title: Position
scenes.situation: The student is breathing and starting to move, but is still very dizzy.

choices.label: Keep them lying on their back and raise their legs
choices.effect: Blood flows back to the brain and they start to feel better.

choices.label: Help them stand up quickly
choices.effect: Standing too soon makes them faint again. They fall and bump their head.

actions.title: Raise legs
actions.instruction: Swipe UP to raise their legs about 30 cm.
actions.hint: Raise the legs, not the head.
actions.success: Blood flows back to the brain.

actions.title: Loosen
actions.instruction: Drag the right action onto the person.
actions.hint: Help them breathe easier and keep cool.

items.label: Crowd around them
items.effect: A crowd blocks the fresh air. They stay dizzy longer.

items.label: Shake them hard
items.effect: Shaking can hurt them and doesn't help them recover.

scenes.title: Recover
scenes.situation: They wake up and say they are thirsty.

choices.label: Let them rest; give a drink only when they are fully alert
choices.effect: They recover safely in the shade.

choices.label: Give food and drink while they are still drowsy
choices.effect: Someone who is not fully awake can choke on food or drink.

tips: Lay the person on their back and raise their legs about 30 cm.
Loosen tight clothing and give them fresh air and shade.
If they are not breathing normally, call 911 and start CPR.
If they don't wake up within a minute or two, call 911.
When they recover, let them sit up slowly. Do not give food or drink until fully alert.

levels.title: Choking
levels.scenario: At lunch, your tito suddenly grabs his throat. He cannot speak, cough or breathe.

scenes.title: Recognize
scenes.situation: Your tito is clutching his throat and cannot make a sound.

choices.label: Ask "Are you choking?" and have someone call 911
choices.effect: He nods - it is a severe blockage. Help is being called while you act.

choices.label: Give him water
choices.effect: Water cannot get past the blockage and can make the choking worse.

choices.label: Sweep his mouth blindly with your finger
choices.effect: A blind finger sweep can push the object deeper into the airway.

actions.title: Get ready
actions.instruction: Tap the actions in the correct order.
actions.hint: Confirm choking, get help, then act.

params.prompt: What do you do, in order?
order: Lean him forward and support his chest

distractors.label: Give him water
distractors.effect: Water cannot get past the blockage and can make the choking worse.

scenes.title: Back blows
scenes.situation: He is leaning forward and still cannot breathe.
scenes.prompt: How do you help clear the airway?

choices.label: Give 5 firm back blows between the shoulder blades
choices.effect: Each firm blow can help loosen the object.

choices.label: Pat him gently on the back
choices.effect: Gentle pats are too weak to move the object. He is running out of air.

actions.title: Back blows
actions.instruction: Give 5 firm back blows: swipe DOWN between the shoulder blades 5 times.
actions.hint: Heel of the hand, firm and downward.

params.wrong_feedback: Back blows go firmly DOWNWARD between the shoulder blades.

scenes.title: Thrusts
scenes.situation: The object is still stuck.

choices.label: Give 5 abdominal thrusts
choices.effect: The quick upward pressure pushes air out of the lungs - the object pops out!

choices.label: Wait and hope it clears
choices.effect: Without air, he can become unconscious within minutes.

actions.title: Abdominal thrusts
actions.instruction: Give 5 abdominal thrusts: swipe UP 5 times (inward and upward).
actions.hint: Fist just above the belly button, pull sharply in and up.
actions.success: The object is out! He can breathe again.

params.wrong_feedback: Abdominal thrusts go sharply INWARD and UPWARD.

tips: If the person can cough forcefully, encourage them to keep coughing.
If they cannot cough, speak or breathe: call 911 (or have someone call).
Give 5 firm back blows between the shoulder blades, then 5 abdominal thrusts. Repeat until the object comes out.
If the person becomes unresponsive, lower them to the ground and start CPR.
Infants and pregnant women need different techniques - learn them in a certified course.

levels.title: Hands-Only CPR
levels.summary: Call 911, push hard and fast in the center of the chest.
levels.scenario: An adult collapses in the barangay hall. They do not respond and are not breathing normally.

scenes.title: Act
scenes.situation: The adult on the floor is not responding and not breathing normally.

choices.label: Call 911, ask for an AED, and start CPR
choices.effect: Help is coming, and CPR keeps blood flowing to the brain until it arrives.

choices.label: Wait to see if they wake up
choices.effect: Without CPR, the brain gets no oxygen. Every minute of waiting lowers the chance of survival.

choices.label: Give them water
choices.effect: An unresponsive person cannot swallow. Water can block the airway.

actions.title: Check & call
actions.instruction: Tap the actions in the correct order.
actions.hint: Safety, response, help, breathing.
actions.success: Help is coming. Now act fast.

params.prompt: What do you do, in order?
order: Make sure the area is safe
Call 911 and ask for an AED

distractors.label: Wait to see if they wake up
distractors.effect: Waiting wastes critical time. Every minute counts.

scenes.title: Hands
scenes.situation: You kneel beside the person.

choices.label: Center of the chest, on the lower half of the breastbone
choices.effect: Pressing here squeezes the heart and pumps blood to the brain.

choices.label: On the stomach
choices.effect: Pushing on the stomach does not pump blood and can cause injury.

actions.title: Hand position
actions.instruction: Drag your hands to the correct spot on the chest.
actions.hint: Center of the chest, lower half of the breastbone.

targets.label: Neck
targets.effect: Pressing on the neck can block the airway and cause injury.

targets.label: Stomach
targets.effect: Pushing on the stomach does not pump blood and can cause injury.

scenes.title: Compress
scenes.situation: Your hands are in place.

choices.label: 100-120 times per minute, hard and fast
choices.effect: Fast, deep compressions keep enough blood moving to protect the brain.

choices.label: Slowly, about once every 2 seconds
choices.effect: Too slow to pump enough blood. The brain is not getting enough oxygen.

actions.title: Compressions
actions.instruction: Tap the chest 30 times at 100-120 per minute. Push hard, push fast!
actions.hint: Follow the blue pulse ring.
actions.success: Keep going until help or an AED arrives!

tips: Check the scene is safe, then tap and shout to check for a response.
Call 911 (Philippines emergency hotline) and ask someone to bring an AED.
Place the heel of your hand on the center of the chest, other hand on top.
Push hard and fast: 100-120 per minute, about 5-6 cm deep.
Let the chest come all the way back up between compressions.
Do not stop until help arrives, an AED is ready, or the person starts breathing.
This game is not a substitute for a certified CPR course.
